intro: On the Turabdin plateau in Mardin province stands Mor Gabriel Monastery, a monastery and church founded in 397. It is the oldest continuously inhabited Syriac Orthodox monastery in the world, and its domed church was given mosaics by Byzantine emperors.
history: Founded in 397, this is the oldest surviving Syriac Orthodox monastery in continuous use. It is named after Gabriel, the bishop who lived here in the seventh century. Look for the mosaics of the main church's dome: they were paid for by Byzantine emperors. And life here goes on, for on the Turabdin plateau the monastery still houses a bishop and a monastic community.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Main church, the Dome mosaics, the House of the Saints and the Monastery court.
facts: Did you know? Turabdin, the plateau the monastery stands on, means 'mountain of the servants of God' in Syriac, and more than eighty monasteries once stood on it. Founded in 397, Mor Gabriel is the oldest Syriac Orthodox monastery still in continuous use.
outro: This brings our tour of Mor Gabriel Monastery to an end. Before you go, please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Thank you for walking with us, and enjoy your visit.
